summary: Adam Air was a privately owned Indonesian airline based in Jakarta. It flew to more than 20 cities in Indonesia, plus Penang and Singapore, and had been the country's fastest-growing low-cost carrier. It was founded in 2002 by Agung Laksono, Speaker of Indonesia's House of Representatives, and Sandra Ang, and began flying in December 2003. Its safety record drew heavy criticism. Pilots reported being pushed to fly unairworthy planes and to break safety rules. Critics said it used political connections to sidestep regulators. After the fatal crash of Flight 574 in January 2007, foreign investors lost interest. In 2008, after another accident and with more than half its fleet seized over missed payments, the government suspended its operating certificate and then revoked it. The airline stopped flying on 18 June 2008. Police later named owner Sandra Ang a suspect in an embezzlement case with reported losses of about US$210 million.
